designs.title: Probably Fine
designs.why: Clean, consistent icon set and a strong deadpan headline; reads like a tidy spec sheet. But in one ink nothing reads as 'lit' — it looks like a reference chart, not a dashboard in crisis, so the joke rests entirely on the caption. The small condensed labels vanish on the tee at 3 m, the dead space under the headline wastes the print area, and the check-engine joke is well-worn territory.
designs.fix: Make the lights look ON: put the icons on a dark dashboard cluster panel (icons knocked out/glowing, with light rays or halos) so the 'everything is warning me' moment lands visually before you read PROBABLY FINE; tighten the bottom whitespace.

designs.title: How to Go to Bed
designs.why: The best of the three: the repetition of 'Turn around.' is a real, specific observation, the pacing from 1 to 7 is a little story, and 'Sigh.' is a perfect payoff. The brush line is loose and warm with genuine character, the serif typography is classy, and it feels like an indie-label tee rather than a meme. Minor: a few stray solid fills on the legs in step 1 and 4 feel accidental, and line weight is on the thin side at chest size.
designs.fix: Thicken the brush strokes ~20% and clean the random solid-black leg patches so the drawings hold up in screen print and read from across a room; keep everything else.

designs.title: The Box
designs.why: The cat-prefers-the-box gag is instantly readable but one of the most familiar cat jokes there is, and the slick, uniform clip-art rendering gives it no voice of its own. Craft issues at full size: the '1' is a malformed glyph that doesn't match the '2' and '3'; in panel 2 the arms' lines run past the right edge of the frame; the bed and box in panel 3 break the frame inconsistently. Dense hatching on the tabby will fill in on a black tee.
designs.fix: Redraw the panel frames and numerals cleanly (consistent '1', no lines leaking past borders, deliberate frame-breaks only), and give it an authorial twist — e.g. the price tag on the bed vs. the box in panel 3 — so it isn't just the stock version of the joke.
